scope: Classify the 16 duplicate-VA groups in manifests/catalog_validation_report.json as legitimate aliases, metadata records sharing a sentinel address, merge candidates, or catalog defects.

inputs: manifests/symbols.json (524-entry symbol catalog; resolved by id lookup)

classification_keys.LEGITIMATE_ALIAS: Multiple BCS-Y entries that should share a VA because the function is intentionally re-tagged from two correct perspectives (e.g., 'vtable slot 1' name + the 'apply method' decomp name; or a dispatcher function + the case-handler records embedded inside it). No action needed; keep all entries.
classification_keys.METADATA_CLUSTER: Several BCS-Y metadata or RTTI/class-marker entries share a known sentinel VA. The collision is catalog bookkeeping rather than a symbol clash.
classification_keys.MERGE_CANDIDATE: Two entries describe the same underlying symbol with redundant data. Should be merged into one record with combined notes.
classification_keys.BUG: One entry is materially wrong - wrong kind, wrong VA, or wrong subject - and should be corrected or removed.

groups.rationale: Both entries describe the same function under two complementary tags. BCS-Y-0045 names it as the slot-1 entry of ChangeActorExtraStatReceiver (vtable perspective from the receiver_classes_inventory.md harvest). BCS-Y-0119 names it as the apply method, with full decomp body details (52 bytes, __thiscall, RTTI cast, tail-calls FUN_006FA980). They are not wrong - they are the same VA tagged twice from two distinct discovery paths (RTTI sweep + decomp sweep). Functional aliasing: vtable slot identity AND apply-method semantics co-exist. Note the address in both records is the same RVA-as-VA bug (the catalog validation report pass's fix is +0x00400000); apply that uniformly when correcting addresses.
groups.recommended_action: Keep both. Optionally cross-link in notes: add 'See companion BCS-Y-0119 apply-method decomp' to BCS-Y-0045 and 'See companion BCS-Y-0045 vtable-slot designation' to BCS-Y-0119. No merge needed; the two perspectives carry different evidence (RTTI source vs Ghidra decomp source).

groups.rationale: Identical pattern to group 1. BCS-Y-0047 is the slot-1 RTTI tag for JobChangeReceiver (from receiver_classes_inventory.md). BCS-Y-0100 is the apply-method decomp with full body (46 bytes, vtable address 0x01057300, dtor pair BCS-Y-0101). Vtable-slot view + apply-method view of the same function VA.

Identical pattern to groups 1 and 2. BCS-Y-0049 is the slot-1 RTTI tag for SetTargetTimeReceiver. BCS-Y-0116 is the apply-method decomp (400-byte body). The two tags arose from independent inventory passes and both correctly point at the same function.
BCS-Y-0092 is the vftable global for LuaActorImpl::vftable. BCS-Y-0241 and BCS-Y-0271 are summary records pinned to the same anchor VA. The overlap is intentional catalog bookkeeping.
groups.recommended_action: Keep BCS-Y-0092 as the canonical vftable entry. Store BCS-Y-0241 and BCS-Y-0271 as metadata rather than symbol records.

groups.rationale: Mixed-perspective alias. BCS-Y-0109 names this function as the AddictLoginTimeKindReceiver::ApplyWrapper (entry slot 12 of the ReceiverApplyWrapperTable). BCS-Y-0161 names it as LuaActorImpl::vftable slot 65 = _onReceiveLimitAddicted. Both are TRUE simultaneously: the AddictLoginTimeKindReceiver apply-wrapper is reached via two distinct dispatch routes - the receiver-apply-wrapper table AND the LuaActorImpl vtable slot 65. BCS-Y-0161's notes explicitly confirm this is the MDI-022 Receiver template (single apply method shared between LuaActorImpl-side wrapper and the Network::*Receiver class).
groups.recommended_action: Keep both. Add reciprocal cross-references in notes so the dual-dispatch nature is documented at the symbol level (currently only documented in BCS-Y-0161).

groups.rationale: BCS-Y-0163 is the canonical Control::MyPlayer::vftable global. BCS-Y-0191 is a partial slot inventory and BCS-Y-0220 is a negative finding pinned to the same address.
groups.recommended_action: Keep BCS-Y-0163 as the canonical vftable global. Store the BCS-Y-0191 inventory and BCS-Y-0220 finding as metadata or documentation rather than symbol records.

groups.rationale: BCS-Y-0164 (kind=global) and BCS-Y-0253 (kind=class) both describe the ExecutePushOnEnterTriggerBoxReceiver vftable / class at 0x00FDFAF8 from two angles: vftable-as-global vs class-as-RTTI-record. They are essentially two facets of the same RTTI artifact. BCS-Y-0264 is the structural-finding summary pinned to the same anchor VA. Address overlap is intentional.
groups.recommended_action: BCS-Y-0264 contains a summary rather than a symbol record. Keep BCS-Y-0164 and BCS-Y-0253 cross-linked because their kind=global and kind=class distinction may be significant. If the catalog adopts one record per class, prefer BCS-Y-0253 because it includes the constructor, apply, and factory chain, and merge BCS-Y-0164's slot-1 layout into it.

The pinning location is arbitrary - the BCS-Y-0218 record covers BCS-Y-0185 AND BCS-Y-0186 (NpcBase, at 0x00FD647C), but is only address-aliased with PlayerBase.

Consider splitting BCS-Y-0218 into two records or moving it to a docs file - it currently has a misleading anchor VA because its content also covers NpcBase. groups.rationale: BCS-Y-0222 summarizes 11 Control namespace classes at the Control::ActorBase vftable VA. BCS-Y-0234 records the canonical ActorBase vftable, including slot 2 dispatch through FUN_00753C30 and ActorBase's outermost actor-tier role. Both summary records use the same VA.
groups.recommended_action: Use BCS-Y-0234 as the canonical ActorBase::vftable global and move BCS-Y-0222's multi-class survey to the architectural findings. BCS-Y-0222 currently occupies a symbol address but contains a survey rather than a symbol record.

groups.rationale: Both entries correctly describe the same function VA from different perspectives. BCS-Y-0238 confirms this is LuaActorImpl::vftable slot 63 firing _onUpdateDisplayName via the third known call path (slots 62/63 form a paired display-name dispatcher). BCS-Y-0252 gives the full decomp body: it is SendLogReceiver's dispatch_wrapper (construct-apply-destruct pattern), reached only via virtual dispatch through LuaActorImpl::vftable[63]. The slot-63 vtable identity + the SendLogReceiver-dispatch-wrapper identity are simultaneously true - the LuaActorImpl slot-63 entry IS the SendLogReceiver dispatch wrapper.
groups.recommended_action: Keep both. Add reciprocal cross-references so the dual identity (vtable-slot view + receiver-dispatch-wrapper view) is explicit in each note. Naming asymmetry is worth flagging: one says '_onUpdateDisplayName' the other says 'SendLogReceiver'. These are not contradictory (the dispatcher fans out to 20 opcodes via the ctor's switch, _onUpdateDisplayName is one of the firer-resolution paths; SendLog is the receiver-class identity).

groups.rationale: BCS-Y-0265 is the canonical ExecuteDebugCommandReceiver class/vftable record (client-internal, not inbound). BCS-Y-0270 is the 'zero remaining gap receivers' structural-finding summary, pinned at the same anchor VA because BCS-Y-0265 was the lone holdout being resolved.
groups.recommended_action: Keep BCS-Y-0265 as the canonical class record. Move BCS-Y-0270's summary to the architectural findings or a catalog note; it currently masquerades as a global at a vftable VA but contains a summary rather than a symbol.

groups.rationale: This group contains legitimate aliases and two metadata records. BCS-Y-0279 and BCS-Y-0321 describe the same central dispatcher from receive and emit-host perspectives. BCS-Y-0525, BCS-Y-0526, and BCS-Y-0527 identify cases within that dispatcher. BCS-Y-0385 and BCS-Y-0386 are catalog summaries rather than globals.
groups.recommended_action: Keep BCS-Y-0279, BCS-Y-0321, and BCS-Y-0525..0527 as legitimate aliases for the dispatcher, emit host, and three case handlers. Move BCS-Y-0385 and BCS-Y-0386 to a catalog-notes manifest because they are worklist and negative-finding records, not functions or globals; kind=global is misleading.

groups.rationale: These two entries describe DIFFERENT things at the same VA, and only one can be correct. BCS-Y-0401 labels FUN_00CD8990 as 'LuaControlLoopFirer' - the engine loop callback firer for the Lua event _onLoop, citing turn6_lua_callbacks.txt and turn12_firer_map.txt. BCS-Y-0501 labels the exact same function as 'LuaEngine_LGEBootstrap' - the Lua Game Engine bootstrap, 1978 bytes, 18 cclosure pushes, embeds a literal Lua wrapper script at .rdata 0x0110e680, installs 13 named globals as C cclosures, sets up the _onLoop userdata metatable with 4 metamethods (__index/__newindex/__eq/__gc), and was resolved via DumpAddrOperandsInFunc.java. The lge bootstrap attribution pass's analysis is far more rigorous (full decomp with literal addresses, defeats decompiler-arg-strip, identifies the exact stdlib overrides, traces the _onLoop metatable installation). The firer-map entry was derived from a CALLBACK HARVEST and likely conflated the bootstrap function with one of its installed metamethods (most plausibly the _onLoop metatable __index/__newindex handler that the bootstrap installs). The BCS-Y-0401 label '_onLoop firer with caller FUN_00CD8990' confuses 'function that installs the _onLoop machinery' (correct - it is the bootstrap) with 'function that fires _onLoop' (incorrect - the actual firer is one of the metamethods FUN_00d08070/FUN_00d085b0/FUN_00d07eb0/FUN_00d08890 installed BY the bootstrap).
groups.recommended_action: Treat BCS-Y-0501 as the authoritative record for FUN_00CD8990. RELABEL BCS-Y-0401 - either (a) remove it and let BCS-Y-0501's notes include the cross-reference to turn6_lua_callbacks.txt's firer-map entry as a corrected attribution, or (b) keep BCS-Y-0401 but change its VA to point at the actual _onLoop firer (one of the 4 metamethods listed in BCS-Y-0501) once it has been positively identified. Either way, the current state where two entries at the same VA disagree on the function's identity needs resolution. Re-read turn6_lua_callbacks.txt + turn12_firer_map.txt against BCS-Y-0501's metamethod list to identify the correct firer VA for the _onLoop callback path.

cross_catalog_notes.catalog_separation: The catalog mixes real symbols with metadata anchored to sentinel VAs. Symbols and metadata require separate record kinds or storage.
